error.codec_experimental_off: %s is experimental, and experimental codecs are turned off on Codecs
error.codec_adaptive_only: Device does not support %s (it only offers aptX Adaptive). Choose aptX Adaptive, Auto, AAC or SBC

error.connect_refused: The device answered but then ended the connection itself. It does not accept a connection right now (for example it is turning off, charging, or connected to another device). Check the device and try again.
error.connect_auth_failed: Authentication failed, also after pairing again. Put the device into pairing mode, or remove the pairing on the device, and try again.

error.aac_unavailable: AAC encoder not available (fdk-aac not built)
error.virtual_capture_init: Failed to initialize capture on virtual device
error.app_capture_unsupported: Application capture needs Windows 11 or Windows 10 version 2004 (build 19041) or later (this PC: build %u). Choose another Capture Source for the device under Audio Devices.
error.no_app_selected: No application selected for Application capture
firmware.title: Bluetooth Firmware Selection
firmware.invalid: %s is not a Realtek firmware file: probably a web page was saved instead of the file. Download it again with the 'plain' link and replace it.
firmware.rom_running: Could not connect: the adapter is running without its Realtek firmware (the files are missing or were not loaded), so it cannot stream. Put the firmware files shown on the Adapter screen into the firmware folder, press Restart Bluetooth and connect again.
firmware.rom_status: The adapter is running its ROM code: the Realtek firmware was not loaded, so it opens but cannot connect or stream. Put the firmware files shown on the Adapter screen into the firmware folder; Bluetooth then starts again with them.
firmware.rom_short: The adapter is running its ROM code: it opens but cannot connect or stream until these files are there.
firmware.manual_instructions:
1. Click 'Open Download Page' to open kernel.org
2. Download the fw and config files
3. Click 'Open Firmware Folder' and place the files there
firmware.vendor_intel: Intel adapter (experimental): no Realtek files needed. If it starts in bootloader mode, place the matching ibt-*.sfi and ibt-*.ddc files from linux-firmware (intel/) in the firmware folder. AX210 and newer are not supported yet.
firmware.vendor_broadcom: Broadcom adapter (experimental): no Realtek files needed. It runs on its ROM firmware; optionally place a PatchRAM file such as BCM20702A1-0b05-17cb.hcd in the firmware folder.
firmware.vendor_csr: CSR adapter: no firmware files needed.
firmware.non_realtek: Realtek initialization is skipped. The adapter runs on its own firmware.
firmware.auto_no_adapter: No adapter detected. Bind it to WinUSB with Zadig; Auto then picks the chip when it is connected.
firmware.auto_unrecognized: The adapter was not recognized. If it has a Realtek chip, choose the chip; otherwise choose Not Realtek.
firmware.vendor_unsupported: This adapter needs a firmware loader that A2DP Windows Bridge does not have (MediaTek / Qualcomm), so A2DP Windows Bridge cannot use it.
firmware.download_explain: A2DP Windows Bridge downloads these files from linux-firmware (kernel.org), checks them and saves them in the firmware folder. They are not included in A2DP Windows Bridge.
firmware.download_license: The files are Realtek's proprietary firmware, redistributable under the terms in linux-firmware's WHENCE and LICENCE.rtlwifi_firmware.txt. Download them only if you accept those terms.
firmware.downloaded: Firmware downloaded. Bluetooth loads it at the next connection.
firmware.downloading: Downloading the firmware from kernel.org… This can take up to a minute.
firmware.download_slow: The download is taking a while. It goes on in the background, and this screen updates when the files are saved.
firmware.download_failed: Could not download the firmware (no connection to kernel.org, or a file did not match). Use Open Download Page to get the files yourself.

profile.empty: No audio device set up yet. Open A2DP Windows Bridge to add one.
profile.name: Name
settings.remember_volume: Remember the Bluetooth Audio Device's Last Volume Level
settings.le_audio_deferred: A2DP Windows Bridge is connected to an audio device or scanning right now. The change takes effect when the next device scan or connection starts.
settings.le_low_latency: Low latency for gaming audio devices (GMAP, experimental)
advanced.max_packet_help:
Upper limit for the audio data in each Bluetooth packet (%d-%d). The audio device's own limit (MTU) always applies too; A2DP Windows Bridge uses the smaller of the two.

%d (recommended) fits one Bluetooth baseband packet. Larger values save only 1-2%% overhead, but more audio is lost when a packet is lost. Applies from the next connection.
debug.capture_failed:
Could not create the HCI capture file:
%s
quality.title: Link Quality
quality.not_streaming: Disconnected. Values appear while audio is being sent.
quality.codec_capped: — limited by the device's maximum bit rate
quality.theory_value: %.0f kbps max, %.1f%% used (3-DH5 back to back)
quality.band_help: Packets occupy 1, 3 or 5 slots whatever their size, so radio time used is higher than the bandwidth share. Above about 80% little room is left for retransmissions and interference easily causes dropouts; lower the quality or turn on ABR in that case.
quality.loss_help: Packets are dropped before sending when the send queue is full (the radio cannot keep up) or L2CAP refuses them. Retransmissions over the air happen inside the Bluetooth controller and are not shown here.
dbgc.flow_hint: Double-click a step to show the log line it came from.
dbgc.audio_idle: No audio playing - nothing to send
dbgc.audio_stalled: Audio captured but no packets sent in the last second
dbgc.mask_tip: Copies show Bluetooth addresses as <addr-1>, <addr-2>... (the adapter's own as <adapter>) and device names as <device-1>, <device-2>...; USB serial numbers, file paths above the app's own folder and your Windows account (user name and SID) are hidden too.
receiver.title: Peer Receiver Test
receiver.intro: Streams to tools/linux_sink/a2dpwb_sink.py on another PC (Linux, ordinary Bluetooth adapter) and compares what was sent with what arrived. The receiver is found on the local network.
receiver.address_hint: empty = find on the local network
receiver.address_tooltip: IP address or host name of the PC running a2dpwb_sink (optionally :port). Empty: find it on the local network (UDP broadcast, port 51201).
receiver.searching: Looking for a receiver on the local network...
receiver.state_failed: Sending failed: %s Check the distance to the receiver and press Start again.
receiver.state_ready: Ready. Start sends to the receiver's Bluetooth adapter.
receiver.state_connecting: Connecting to the receiver over Bluetooth...
receiver.state_waiting: Waiting for audio to arrive at the receiver...
receiver.mtu_tooltip: MTU the receiver offers for the media channel: 672 as BlueZ, 679 the smallest LDAC accepts, 895 / 1005 common in audio devices. Applies from Start.
receiver.log_start: Start: send %s, %s, %s, %s, %s to %s; receiver MTU %s, buffer %s
receiver.log_configure_failed: the receiver did not confirm the settings (older a2dpwb_sink?)
receiver.log_link_lost: Bluetooth connection lost, A2DP Windows Bridge reconnects
receiver.source_tooltip: Test tone (1 kHz left / 1.5 kHz right) keeps the stream steady. System audio sends what the PC plays; while it plays nothing, nothing is sent, and the receiver counts that as a pause.
receiver.afh_tooltip: Channels Bluetooth should avoid (AFH host classification, applies to every connection): Auto = the 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi channel this PC is connected on (nothing when it is not on 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi), Off = leave it to the Bluetooth controller, Manual = the Wi-Fi channels entered, e.g. 6,11. At least 20 of the 79 channels stay in use.
receiver.help: Counts start with each stream and at Reset. Lost = gaps in the RTP sequence numbers (classic aptX and aptX LL carry none). The receiver models a sink with the buffer shown: a dropout is when it would have run dry, a skip when a burst after a stall would have overfilled it.
tray.minimized_hint: A2DP Windows Bridge is still running in the system tray.
update.error:

update.balloon: A2DP Windows Bridge %s is available. Click here to open the download page.
capture.auto_switch: Auto Switch Windows Default Audio Output Device
capture.volume_sync_hint: The audio device's volume and the Windows volume move together.
capture.app_hint: Lists the apps that are playing audio. If yours is missing, start playback in it and click Refresh.
capture.hint_loopback: Records what the Windows default output device plays: all apps mixed. It keeps playing on that device too.
capture.hint_virtual: Records what apps play into the selected device.
capture.hint_app: Records only what the selected app (and its child processes) plays, after the app's own processing. The app keeps playing on its output device too.
tooltip.quality: Encoding quality level. Higher quality uses more bandwidth.
tooltip.abr: Adaptive Bit Rate: auto-adjusts quality based on connection stability (LDAC and LHDC V5). LHDC V5 ABR stays at 400 kbps or below (as on Android) and ignores the quality setting.
tooltip.codec_fallback_help:
The device did not offer %s when connecting, so %s is used instead.

Sony audio devices (e.g. WH-1000XM4): LDAC is not offered while "Connect to 2 devices simultaneously" (multipoint) is on. Turn it off in the Sony Sound Connect (Headphones Connect) app, then connect again. Some models, such as the WH-1000XM6, support LDAC together with multipoint.

If the audio device is also connected to a phone or another PC, disconnect it there and connect again.
tooltip.sample_rate: Audio sample rate. Auto: 48 kHz, or the best rate the audio device takes if it has no 48 kHz. Higher rates use more bandwidth and may add latency.
tooltip.bit_depth: Audio bit depth. 24-bit provides higher dynamic range (LDAC and LHDC V5).
volume.label: Volume
tooltip.volume: The audio device's volume (AVRCP absolute volume), kept for each device. It also follows the volume buttons on the audio device, and the Windows volume chosen in its Windows Volume Sync on Audio Devices. Shown when the audio device supports it.
tooltip.auto_switch: Automatically set the capture source device as the Windows default output while connected.
tooltip.media_keys: Allows the Bluetooth audio device's buttons to play/pause/resume and skip tracks.
ui.nav.label: Main
ui.nav.toggle: Show or hide the menu labels
ui.dev.intro: For finding out why a device stays silent. Changes apply when the next stream starts. Everything is off by default.
ui.dev.active: Overrides are on. Turn them off before reporting a problem, or say which are on: they are in the log.
ui.dev.rtp_marker_hint: Sets the marker bit in every media packet.
ui.dev.packet_dump_hint: Writes the size, timestamp and first bytes of the first media packets to the log.
ui.dev.aac_config_bitrate0_hint: Sends 0 (unknown) as the bit rate when it configures the audio device.
ui.dev.aac_latm_v0_hint: AudioMuxVersion 0 with implicit signaling, instead of the format Android and PipeWire send.
ui.dev.aac_bitrate_hint: 32 to 512; empty = the highest bit rate the device takes. Still limited by the media payload.
ui.dev.log_intro: How the core logs while developer mode is on. Turning developer mode off goes back to the defaults.
ui.dev.log_keep_days_hint: 1 to 365 (default 7). Older daily files of the core and the window are removed now and each day.
ui.dev.log_day_cap_hint: 10 to 10240 (default 100). When a day's file reaches it, debug and trace lines stop until the next day; info and above go on.
ui.dev.log_always_hint: No 24-hour or 1-hour limit, and in force from the core's start (problems at start-up). Diagnostics' switch can still raise it.
ui.dev.log_trace_warn: Trace logs every HCI and media packet: hundreds of MB an hour, up to the daily size limit.
ui.dev.log_health_hint: Logs the stream health line every interval for the whole stream, not only in its first minute, so stutter can be compared between sessions.
ui.dev.mark_hint: Puts a numbered marker line in the log, to find the moment again (e.g. when the stutter starts).
ui.conn.connecting: Connecting to the A2DP Windows Bridge core...
ui.conn.missing_title: The A2DP Windows Bridge core is not running
ui.conn.missing_body: a2dpwb-core.exe streams the audio and must run next to this window. It could not be started; reinstalling A2DP Windows Bridge puts it back. This window keeps trying to connect.
ui.conn.rejected_title: The core is a different version
ui.conn.rejected_body: This window and a2dpwb-core.exe come from different versions of A2DP Windows Bridge. Install the same version of both (installing the latest release does this).
ui.volume.unknown: Not reported by the audio device
ui.codec.lc3_desc: The best LC3 configuration the device offers
ui.error.copied: The error and the diagnostic log were copied to the clipboard (Bluetooth addresses masked)
ui.error.copy_hint: Copy the error with the diagnostic info and recent log, to paste into a report
ui.error.report_hint: Open a GitHub issue with this error and the diagnostic info filled in
ui.error.report_opened: GitHub opened in your browser with the error and the diagnostic info filled in. Add what you were doing; the full log is also on the clipboard.
ui.crash.title: A2DP Windows Bridge stopped unexpectedly
ui.crash.when: %s, %s. It was started again; a report helps fix the cause.
ui.devices.manual_hint: The audio device's Bluetooth address, if the scan does not find it
ui.device.forget_confirm: Remove this device from the saved devices? Its codec settings are kept.
ui.profile.quality_highest_hint: The highest bit rate the audio device takes. ABR or VBR, where offered, lets it vary.
ui.profile.err_device: Choose the audio device (add it under Audio Devices first)
ui.profile.codecs_unknown: Which codecs the audio device supports is known after its first connection.
ui.profile.codec_settings_apply: OK chooses %s for this audio device.
ui.profile.le_audio_unsupported: This Bluetooth adapter cannot stream LE Audio (no isochronous channels).
ui.profile.le_audio_unchecked: Not known yet whether this Bluetooth adapter can stream LE Audio: it is checked the first time A2DP Windows Bridge uses it (a scan or a connection). Until then LE Audio counts as unsupported.
ui.profile.format_differs: The audio device streams with another %s. Set the capture source to the same format in Windows' Sound settings to avoid a conversion.
ui.profile.app_capture_requirement: Needs Windows 11 or Windows 10 version 2004 (build 19041) or later.
ui.profile.app_capture_unsupported: Not available on this PC: needs Windows 11 or Windows 10 version 2004 (build 19041) or later.
ui.diag.copied: Diagnostic information copied to the clipboard
ui.diag.bundle_tip: One .zip with the logs, crash reports, system information and HCI captures, to attach to a report.
ui.diag.bundle_dialog_text: The bundle collects the logs, crash reports, system information (adapters, drivers, audio devices) and settings. Link keys are never included.
ui.diag.bundle_hci_hint: The Bluetooth traffic of the last minutes and of failed connections. Very helpful for connection problems. Contains Bluetooth addresses and device names (not the pairing keys). Leave it off unless you were asked for them.
ui.diag.bundle_mask_hint: In the logs and the other text files. The HCI captures keep the addresses.
ui.diag.bundle_attach: Attach this file to your GitHub issue.
ui.diag.bundle_too_big: Larger than GitHub's 25 MB limit for attachments: send it by email or another file service instead.
ui.diag.report_opened: GitHub opened in your browser with the details filled in. Drag the bundle from Explorer into the issue; the diagnostic info is also on the clipboard.
ui.diag.bundle_tip: One .zip with the logs, HCI captures, crash reports and system information, to attach to a report
ui.diag.bundle_failed:
Could not save the diagnostic bundle:
%s
ui.diag.bundle_attach: Attach this file to your GitHub issue. HCI captures (hci/) contain your Bluetooth addresses.
ui.diag.verbose_until: On until %s, then off by itself. Reproduce the problem, then save a diagnostic bundle.
ui.diag.verbose_help: Turn it on before reproducing a problem: it stays on for 24 hours, also across restarts.
error.bundle_failed: Could not save the diagnostic bundle: %s
ui.diag.line_gone: That line is no longer in the log
ui.diag.iso_help: Since the LE Audio stream was set up. An SDU set carries one frame for every stream. When the buffer runs empty, silence is sent and more frames are buffered before sending.
ui.diag.cd_no_device: The device did not report these capabilities
ui.diag.cd_legend: Filled: in use. Outlined: offered by the device. Faded: not offered.
ui.diag.cd_help: From the capabilities the device reported (AVDTP) and the configuration A2DP Windows Bridge sent.
ui.diag.cd_bitpool_help: The bitpool sets how many bits each SBC frame gets: the higher, the better the sound and the higher the bit rate. The device accepts the range it lists; the configuration may narrow it.
ui.diag.cd_bitpool_abr_help: Under ABR the bitpool drops by 2 when the send queue backs up (at most every 0.5 s) and climbs back by 1 per second once it has drained; the frames and the bit rate shrink and grow with it.
ui.receiver.none_found: No receiver answered on the local network.
ui.receiver.afh_hint: Channel hopping (AFH) applies to every connection: it is set on the Adapter screen.
ui.adapter.status_stopped: Stopped (starts with the first scan or connection)
ui.adapter.none_hint: Plug in a USB Bluetooth adapter, then press Refresh. A2DP Windows Bridge needs its own adapter, separate from the PC's built-in Bluetooth.
ui.adapter.ids_unknown: The address and Bluetooth version show once Windows' Bluetooth or A2DP Windows Bridge has used this adapter (Windows' Bluetooth uses only one adapter at a time)
ui.adapter.experimental_hint: Support for this vendor's adapters is experimental: it has been tried on only a few adapters so far.
ui.adapter.assign_title: Let A2DP Windows Bridge use this adapter
ui.adapter.assign_explain: A2DP Windows Bridge drives the adapter itself through the WinUSB driver (part of Windows). While it is assigned, Windows' own Bluetooth no longer sees this adapter: devices paired with Windows through it stop working until you restore the driver. Other Bluetooth adapters (for example the PC's built-in one) are not affected.
ui.adapter.assign_short: Replaces the original driver: Windows will no longer use this adapter for Bluetooth
ui.adapter.assign_unsupported: A2DP Windows Bridge cannot use this adapter, so its driver stays as it is
ui.adapter.restore_title: Give the adapter back to Windows
ui.adapter.restore_explain: Windows picks its own driver for the adapter again, and Windows' Bluetooth can use it. A2DP Windows Bridge cannot stream through it until WinUSB is assigned again.
ui.adapter.restore_short: Gives the adapter back to Windows' Bluetooth
ui.adapter.uac_note: Windows asks for administrator permission (UAC) to change the driver.
ui.adapter.assigned_restart: %s now uses the WinUSB driver, but Windows loads it only after a restart of the adapter: unplug it and plug it back in (a built-in adapter: restart Windows) before connecting.
ui.adapter.restart_needed_hint: Windows has not loaded the driver yet. Unplug the adapter and plug it back in; for a built-in adapter, restart Windows.
ui.adapter.restored: %s is back on its original driver
ui.adapter.afh_channels_hint: Wi-Fi channels 1 to 14, separated by commas, e.g. 6,11
ui.adapter.afh_bad: Enter Wi-Fi channels from 1 to 14, e.g. 6,11
ui.settings.start_minimized_logon: When A2DP Windows Bridge starts with Windows: on, only the tray icon appears; off, the main window opens.
ui.settings.tray_click_opens_window: Clicking the tray icon opens the full app window
ui.settings.tray_click_opens_window_hint: Off: a click opens the small tray window.
ui.settings.notify_connected_hint: Shows the device, its codec with the sample rate, bit depth and bit rate, and the battery if known.
ui.update.waiting: Version %s is downloaded. It is installed when the audio device disconnects.
ui.update.streaming: The update waits until the audio device disconnects.
ui.update.installing: Installing version %s. A2DP Windows Bridge starts again by itself.
ui.update.failed: The update could not be installed (%s). The release page has the installer.
ui.update.portable: This copy is portable: get the new version from the release page.
ui.update.unsigned: This build does not update itself: get the new version from the release page.
ui.settings.developer_mode_hint: Adds the Developer screen (receiver test, overrides) and more details to the log. No restart needed.
ui.settings.le_low_latency_hint: Shorter delay for gaming audio devices that support it. Applies from the next LE Audio connection.
ui.settings.run_setup_hint: The first-run steps: adapter, driver and firmware, audio devices
ui.settings.icons_license: Icons: Fluent UI System Icons (MIT License, Microsoft).
ui.settings.quit_hint: Disconnects the audio device and closes the tray icon
ui.settings.quit_confirm: The audio device disconnects and A2DP Windows Bridge closes completely, including the tray icon.
ui.setup.title: Set up A2DP Windows Bridge
ui.setup.intro: Three steps to hear your PC on your audio devices.
ui.setup.adapter_intro: A2DP Windows Bridge needs a USB Bluetooth adapter of its own. Choose the one to use.
ui.setup.unsupported_note: A2DP Windows Bridge does not support this adapter: it cannot load the firmware of MediaTek and Qualcomm chips. Choose a supported adapter, such as a Realtek one.
ui.setup.driver_ok: The adapter is ready for A2DP Windows Bridge
ui.setup.auto_explain: A2DP Windows Bridge needs this adapter to itself. One click sets it up:
ui.setup.auto_will_driver: Switches it to the WinUSB driver. Windows then stops using this adapter, so devices paired with Windows through it stop working until you give it back on the Adapters screen. Other adapters, such as the PC's built-in one, keep working.
ui.setup.auto_driver: Switching the driver… Windows may ask for permission.
ui.setup.auto_failed: The adapter could not be set up
ui.setup.auto_advanced: To do these steps one by one (driver, firmware, manual download), use the Adapters screen.
ui.setup.device_intro: Put the audio device in pairing mode and press Connect next to it. A2DP Windows Bridge picks the best settings for it and connects.
ipc.error.not_connected: Not connected to the A2DP Windows Bridge core
ipc.error.disconnected: The connection to the A2DP Windows Bridge core was lost
ipc.error.timeout: The A2DP Windows Bridge core did not answer (%s)
ipc.error.rfcomm_not_connected: The device is not connected to A2DP Windows Bridge
ipc.error.rfcomm_service_not_found: The device does not offer this service
ipc.error.rfcomm_open_failed: The RFCOMM channel could not be opened (%s)
ipc.error.rfcomm_busy: The RFCOMM channel is busy, try again
ipc.error.rfcomm_timeout: No answer from the RFCOMM channel in time; it may or may not have been done. Open the channel again
error.profile_save: The settings could not be saved
error.settings_save: The settings could not be saved
error.profile_not_found: This audio device is not saved any more
error.device_forget: The device could not be removed from the list
error.device_rename: The device could not be renamed

error.capture_start: The HCI capture could not be started

error.driver_failed: Changing the driver failed. See the log for details.
error.driver_assign_failed: Windows refused to assign WinUSB to this adapter. Install it with Zadig instead (see "Using Zadig instead" in the setup guide); details are in the log.
error.driver_restore_unverified: The driver was changed, but the adapter did not return to its previous driver. If it was set up with Zadig, remove Zadig's driver package in Device Manager.
ui.v1_running.title: Another A2DP Windows Bridge is running — exit it first
ui.v1_running.text: Two copies of A2DP Windows Bridge (v1, or another v2) cannot use the Bluetooth adapter at the same time. Right-click the other A2DP Windows Bridge's tray icon and choose Exit.
help.third_party: Also includes libldac (Apache-2.0), libopenaptx (LGPL-2.1+, © 2017 Aurelien Jacobs, © 2018-2020 Pali Rohár), Fraunhofer FDK AAC, Bluedroid SBC (Apache-2.0), the LHDC V5 encoder (Apache-2.0, derived from AOSP; FFT from KISS FFT, BSD-3-Clause), libopus (BSD-3-Clause), liblc3 (Apache-2.0), Tauri, SolidJS and other Rust and JavaScript libraries. License texts are in the "licenses" folder next to the program.
tooltip.vbr: Variable bit rate AAC: the encoder spends bits where the music needs them. Used only if the audio device lists VBR; otherwise the bit rate stays constant. Takes effect when AAC is chosen by name (not Auto).
tooltip.sbc_bitpool: How many bits each SBC frame gets: higher sounds better and needs a higher bit rate (%d-%d). Auto: the highest. The audio device's own range always applies.
tooltip.sbc_abr: Adaptive bitpool: lowers the SBC bitpool when the connection falls behind and raises it again step by step once it keeps up, between the bitpool chosen and the lowest one that still sounds good. Off: the bitpool stays fixed. Applies when SBC or SBC XQ is chosen for the device, not under Auto-select or a fallback.
tooltip.sbc_bitpool_live: SBC bitpool in use / the stream's highest. ABR moves it between %u and %u as the connection allows.
error.sbc_bitpool_range: Enter a bitpool from %d to %d, or Auto
ui.devices.page_hint: Scan, add and manage Bluetooth audio devices like headphones, speakers and earbuds.
ui.devices.saved_empty: No saved devices yet. Add one under Audio Devices.
ui.home.battery_refused_tip: The headphones refused to report their battery. Another device (such as a phone) may be connected to them at the same time; disconnect it and reconnect to see the battery.
ui.home.no_device: No audio device yet. Add one to get started.
ui.profile.sbc_frame_hint: Blocks, subbands, bit allocation and channel mode of each SBC frame. Auto keeps 16 blocks, 8 subbands, Loudness and Joint stereo (SBC XQ: dual channel). Only what the audio device supports is listed; a value it does not take falls back to Auto when connecting.
ui.profile.sbc_bitpool_handles: Left handle: the lowest bitpool, where ABR stops lowering it. Right handle: the highest, the one the stream starts with.
status.device_back: The audio device is back on, connecting...
ui.profile.codecs_hide_hint: Disable to show both supported and unsupported codecs
ui.codecs.auto_select: Auto-select the codec with the highest quality
ui.codecs.auto_select_hint: Disable to allow manual codec selection, configuration and order
ui.codecs.auto_dialog_text: To customize codec configuration and order, Auto-select must be disabled.
ui.codecs.settling: Switching the codec. Wait a moment before choosing another.
ui.codecs.order_keys: Drag the codec cards, or press Alt with an arrow key on a card, to change the audio device's order. A codec the device does not support falls back to the first card it supports.
ui.profile.sbc_quality_hint: The bit rate the bitpool and frame setup below give (at 48 kHz when the rate is Auto, or 44.1 kHz on an audio device without 48 kHz).
ui.devices.none_saved: No audio devices yet. Scan for yours or add it by its address below.
